skill.name: ccxt
skill.description: Use CCXT documentation to build cryptocurrency exchange integrations, retrieve market data, manage orders, and troubleshoot trading API behavior in JavaScript, Python, and PHP.
skill.summary: Guides CCXT exchange API development for market data, order management, WebSockets, authentication, and rate limits.
skill.author: 2025Emma

content.value_statement: Developers need reliable guidance when working across many crypto exchange APIs. This skill organizes CCXT documentation for integration, trading workflows, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains CCXT setup paths for JavaScript, Python, PHP, browser bundles, Docker, and source builds.
Summarizes exchange capabilities, market loading, rate limits, API credentials, and sandbox mode.
Guides unified methods for market data, orders, balances, deposits, withdrawals, and fees.
Covers CCXT Pro WebSocket concepts, streaming subscriptions, caches, and async usage.
Points users to reference files for CLI usage, exchanges, certification, and detailed manual topics.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not a trading bot or financial advice.
It does not verify exchange availability, fees, laws, or live market conditions.
It does not protect users from losing funds through incorrect code or credentials.
It does not include executable helper scripts or automated tests.

use_cases.title: Plan market data integration
use_cases.description: Implement a unified market data integration across supported exchanges using CCXT patterns and rate limit guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare private API workflows
use_cases.description: Review order, balance, and funding workflows before adding private API calls to an automated system.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot exchange API errors
use_cases.description: Diagnose API errors by checking required credentials, exchange capabilities, verbose logs, and known CCXT exception types.

prompt_templates.title: Start with public data
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup and first read-only request
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install CCXT for Python and fetch basic public market data for one exchange. Explain each step.

prompt_templates.title: Select unified methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Map a feature need to CCXT methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the correct CCXT unified method for balances, open orders, and recent trades on an exchange.

prompt_templates.title: Review private endpoint design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CCXT integration plan for rate limits, sandbox mode, API credentials, and error handling before I connect private endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design streaming architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CCXT Pro WebSocket architecture for several exchanges. Include subscription flow, cache behavior, reconnection handling, and pagination boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need to retrieve recent trades from several exchanges without breaking limits.
output_examples.output: The response explains when to use unified trade methods, why pagination matters, and how to reuse exchange instances with rate limits enabled.

output_examples.input: My private order call fails with an API key error.
output_examples.output: The response checks credentials, permissions, sandbox mode, nonce behavior, and exchange-specific requirements before suggesting next debugging steps.

output_examples.input: I want streaming order books for a trading dashboard.
output_examples.output: The response maps CCXT Pro watch methods, cache limits, reconnection behavior, and cases where REST polling remains necessary.

best_practices: Keep API keys scoped, private, and out of shared logs or support requests.
Reuse exchange instances and keep rate limiting enabled unless you fully control throttling.
Use sandbox mode before any private trading workflow touches real funds.
anti_patterns: Sharing apiKey or secret values in issues, chats, screenshots, or verbose logs.
Creating a new exchange instance for every request under the same API key.
Using market orders or withdrawals without validating symbols, amounts, fees, and networks.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps with CCXT documentation and integration planning. Users must execute and review their own code.

faq.question: Can it provide financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It explains library behavior and API usage. It does not recommend assets, positions, or strategies.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CCXT concepts for JavaScript, Python, PHP, browser builds, and related async patterns.

faq.question: Does it support CCXT Pro?
faq.answer: Yes. The included references discuss WebSocket subscriptions, caches, watch methods, and async streaming behavior.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys?
faq.answer: Use restricted keys, avoid sharing secrets, and test permissions in sandbox mode where exchanges support it.

faq.question: Can it debug exchange errors?
faq.answer: It can guide troubleshooting using verbose logs, exception classes, required credentials, and exchange-specific documentation.
